$comment: Spec 120 §3.4 — the INTERPRETATION file for enrich_permits, capped at 12 prose entries (notes-cap.mjs).
Phase-4 wave 4 lane B commit ② (2026-10-18). One of the two notes files of the ONE shared lead-zoning
compute module (scripts/lib/enrich-lead-zoning.js); its twin carries the same module facts for the
other target. Every measured block was read against the dev DB on 2026-10-18 (read-only session).

read_this_way.what: enrich_permits is one of two slugs over ONE compute module (operator-approved 2026-10-18, wave-4 plan question 9). The target is selected by the descriptor identity (identity.name -> target in TARGET_OF), never by an environment variable: the legacy ENRICH_TARGET selector retires with the ③ shell swap. The two slugs run in different chains (permits / coa), share advisory lock 66, and are independent steps with independent goldens.

measured.value: scripts/lib/compute/enrich-permits.js is one line over the shared module; the legacy scripts/enrich-permits.js served both slugs through process.env.ENRICH_TARGET (:601).

read_this_way.what: The max-build, existing-structure, scenario, optimal-config and cost columns on permits are a COPY of the dominant linked parcel's enrich_parcels outputs (Spec 65, Spec 78 §4D), not a lead-level computation: max_build_confidence degrades to 'low' when a lead links more than one parcel (no coherent envelope on an assembly). Every lead-level consumer of those columns depends on this copy staying exact; the conversion keeps it byte-identical (operator brief 2026-10-18).

measured.value: run 1570 (2026-07-17): scope 254,082, updated 40,725, coverage 84.1 % PASS, no-link 13,899, multi-parcel 989, heterogeneous 503, fsi-null 83 % (floor 88), coverage-null 66.2 % (floor 72).
measured.query: SELECT id, started_at, records_total, records_updated, records_meta->'audit_table'->'rows' FROM pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline = 'permits:enrich_permits' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 5

known_normal.what: permits_zoning_class_coverage_pct sits around 84-87 % — the structural ceiling (about 5.5 % of leads have no parcel link, about 10 % link a gap parcel with no zoning). Spec 66 DEC-5 calibrated the FAIL floor at 80 and the PASS floor at 83 against it; a reading in that band is health, not degradation.

measured.value: run 1570 (2026-07-17): scope 254,082, updated 40,725, coverage 84.1 % PASS, no-link 13,899, multi-parcel 989, heterogeneous 503, fsi-null 83 % (floor 88), coverage-null 66.2 % (floor 72).
measured.query: SELECT id, started_at, records_total, records_updated, records_meta->'audit_table'->'rows' FROM pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline = 'permits:enrich_permits' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 5

known_bad.what: Coverage below the fail floor (enrich_permits_zoning_coverage_fail_pct) means the upstream link (link_parcels) or enrich_parcels' zoning pass regressed, not that this step is wrong: this step copies what is linked.

measured.value: No FAIL in the recorded history of either slug (latest runs PASS).
measured.query: SELECT id, started_at, records_total, records_updated, records_meta->'audit_table'->'rows' FROM pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline = 'permits:enrich_permits' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 5

blind_spots.what: The F-H12 gate measures zoning_class coverage only. The other ~120 propagated columns have INFO population counts and no bound, so a regression that blanks, say, the cost columns on a still-linked lead shows only as an INFO count falling.

measured.value: checks[]: one FAIL-capable row (coverage), two WARN-capable null floors (plus the two permit_type disagreement rows on permits), every other row INFO.

suspicious_if.signal: permits_unlink_cleared_count is large. The orphan nullify resets only leads that lost ALL their permit_parcels rows; a large number means the link table lost rows upstream. Check the generated before image (recovery.before_image) before re-running: after the nullify commits the prior feed values exist nowhere else.

measured.query: SELECT id, started_at, records_total, records_updated, records_meta->'audit_table'->'rows' FROM pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline = 'permits:enrich_permits' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 5

decisions.what: The lineage and centreline-coverage preconditions stay named HALTs inside the enrich pass (the enrich_centreline assertCentrelineNonEmpty precedent): they read parcels, not the run ledger. The centreline recency read moved to the contract_read hook through the runner producer reader, which returns the two stamps and never throws (R-BZ G1/G8); the 16 catalog probes became database.min_migration (G3). Drafted deviations, operator ruling owed at integration.
The legacy zero-denominator row (permits_construction_count_zero) now renders on every run (false on a normal run): a declared check always produces a row. Declared diff.

fences.const: the dominant-parcel pick ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY <lead> ORDER BY par.lot_size_sqm DESC NULLS LAST, <link>.confidence DESC NULLS LAST, par.id ASC) and the jsonb_agg(... ORDER BY area_share DESC NULLS LAST, parcel_id)
fences.incident: Without the explicit ORDER BY the jsonb arrays come back in heap order and the IS DISTINCT FROM guard rewrites every multi-parcel lead on every run (the WF2 float/jsonb idempotency lesson, Spec 66 §2).

fences.const: the orphan nullify resets the NOT NULL booleans to false (set_value false), never NULL
fences.incident: NULLing a NOT NULL boolean crashes the whole statement (PG 23502) and with it the shared transaction — the ravine, heritage, centreline and max-build propagations each had to add their booleans to the false list.

fences.const: zoning_enriched_at stays OUT of the UPDATE guard
fences.incident: A run-clock column inside an IS DISTINCT FROM guard makes the guard vacuous (LG-9/D-5): every lead would be rewritten every run.

review_notes.what: Phase-4 wave 4 lane B ② (2026-10-18): compute ported, shell still legacy (stage compute_ported). PRE captures on the legacy shell (night P3) precede the ③ shell swap; the POST + forced bracket ride night P4 in chain order.
